then.text: You've got the Neanderthal facts. Take them up to the Upper Rock and tell the Cave Warden.

else.text: The skull found in Forbes' Quarry in 1848 is called Gibraltar 1. It was the first adult Neanderthal skull ever found, and nobody knew what it was for eight years.

The Neanderthals lived on the Rock for a very long time, some say until around 30,000 years ago. Gorham's Cave has their hearths, and a patch of rock they scratched with a pattern that looks like hashtags. Go and tell the Cave Warden at St Michael's Cave that you've seen it.
Welcome to the Gibraltar Museum. Mind the baths: they are 14th century, very old and very arched, and they've got a lot of steps down.
If you'd like a project, the Cave Warden at St Michael's Cave is looking for someone who knows the Rock's early story. Have a look round, then go and see them.

gib_baths.text: The Moorish baths were hidden under later buildings for centuries. They were uncovered when the house above was being rebuilt.
The arches are horseshoe-shaped. If you're going to look at one thing, look at the roof. It has little star-shaped holes for the steam to escape.
